def get_collision_reward(self):
        """
        Added in Version-SOP.
        """
        pursuer_position_matrix = self.pursuer_layer.get_state_matrix()

        if self.surround:
            # No collisions are allowed
            evader_position_matrix = self.evader_layer.get_state_matrix()
            all_agents_positions_matrix = pursuer_position_matrix + evader_position_matrix
        else:
            # Collisions with evaders are allowed, while that with other pursuers are prevented.
            all_agents_positions_matrix = pursuer_position_matrix

        collisions = [all_agents_positions_matrix[self.pursuer_layer.get_position(agent_id)[0],
                                                  self.pursuer_layer.get_position(agent_id)[1]] - 1
                      for agent_id in range(self.n_pursuers)]

        self.n_agents_collide_with_others_per_multiagent_step = np.count_nonzero(collisions)
        self.n_collision_events_per_multiagent_step = np.count_nonzero(np.maximum(all_agents_positions_matrix - 1, 0))

        collision_rewards = self.collision_reward * np.asarray(collisions)

        self.n_collision_with_obstacles = np.sum([pursuer.collide_with_obstacle for pursuer in self.pursuers])

        return collision_rewards

Hi, 

0. First, The stp_rl_pursuer_6_6_4_1_.txt is an outdated result that is trained with A2C using a different reward function. This result is abandoned because we found that the reward function used is not suitable for the training with more than one evaders. Hence, we change that reward function to the current one, which performs good for the cases of multiple evaders. 

1. As for the training epochs, for the simplest case of 4 pursuers vs. 1 static evader, 1000 training epochs are sufficient to observe the convergence. But for complex cases, such as with more evaders, stronger evaders, and in bigger environments, more epochs are needed. For example, for multiple static or random-walking evaders, 5000 epochs are sufficient for A2C.
2. The for_scope is always 11, the default value.
3. sop_40_40_4_1_.txt is the newest result with the current reward function.

Best regards!

Hi, 

1. The hyper parameters in the codes, such as train_sop_actor_critic.py and train_sop_mappo.py,  are exactly the ones that we used for the results in the paper.
2. As for the hyperparameters you provided, steps_per_epoch=8000 may be a little large because it means 8000 * 4 = 32000 training samples will be generated per epoch for the case of 4 pursuer.
4. n_epochs = 1000 is not enough for the surrounding based capture. Sorry, the last time I said 1000 epochs is sufficient is for the occupying-based capture, such as the pettingzoo pursuit environment, which is the self-orgainizing search task (multi_target_self_organizing_search) in our work.
5. In the multi_target_self_organizing_pursuit/data/log_actor_critic/pursuit_epoch2000x14.gif, and multi_target_self_organizing_pursuit/data/log_mappo/sop_mappo/test_sop_mappo.gif, we render our training results for A2C and MAPPO, for your reference. 
6. For your "not good result", we can discuss more. According to our experience, it is not easy to achieve perfect surrounding based capture strictly under the setup of POSG (partially observable stochastic game) where simultaneous decisions are made after the simultaneous observations of agents, especially in an implicit coordination way (no communication, no full observation). The perfect I mean here is in terms of the efficiency, obstacle avoidance, and multi-agent collision avoidance. Our current result is for your reference. And our current reward function may not be the best, although workable. 

We are pleased to be responsible for the reproductivity of our work and discuss related research problems.
You are welcome to contact us by: Lijun.Sun@student.uts.edu.au, 11860004@mail.sustech.edu.cn, or sunlijun522@126.com.

Best regards.

Hi, 
Again thank you for your comprehensive answer. I really really appreciate that.

Hi, 
1. the (self-organizing search) environment is designed in this way. When an agent collides with an obstacle, e.g., a boundary, it will die in its location.
2. If you want a less restricted search environment where an agent will be penalised by reward if it collides with obstacles but will keep alive and continue the game, we recommend the Pursuit-Evasion-O environment of our new work in https://github.com/LijunSun90/MatrixWorld. If you want to compare with our algorithm, you can continue use the current repository, or our new environment. We will integrate our algorithm FSC2 in that new repository soon.
3. If there are other problems, you are welcome to contact us.

The agent-agent collision is defined as that more than one agents exist in one position of the matrix (grid world). And the total number of collisions occur in one time step is the summation of all collisions in all positions.

You can refererence our experimental result https://github.com/LijunSun90/pursuitFSC2/blob/main/multi_target_self_organizing_search/results/sos_MADDPG/result_Time(s).png for MADDPG on SOS (self-organizing search).
From our records, our training time is relative stable.

The ApexDQN algorithm is based on the Ray library. If the status is always PENDING, it means the training does not run at all. It is recommended to run on a workstation or server, rather than a PC or laptop. To fit your computation resources, parameters in line 57-59 of train_sos_apexdqn.py need to be adjusted accordingly.
